inputs.original_text: I just heard about Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, being convicted in Paris under the new law targeting psychological subjection. While some are framing this as an attack on the Church and traditional values by elites, it's really a necessary pushback against the institutional power that religious authorities have long used to exert control over vulnerable people. These structures have historically reinforced inequality, suppressed dissent, and prioritized rigid hierarchies over individual rights and equality. Holding leaders accountable like this is a step toward protecting marginalized groups from manipulation and reforming systems that have shielded abuse for far too long.
inputs.modified_text: This conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, in Paris under the new law targeting psychological subjection shows the kind of accountability long overdue against religious institutions that have wielded unchecked power to dominate vulnerable people. These hierarchies have for generations entrenched inequality, crushed resistance, and placed rigid control above basic rights, shielding exploitation while harming the most marginalized. Far from any attack on tradition, this is essential reform to dismantle those oppressive systems and defend communities from manipulation.
